name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28 in the BTK PH domain contacts the inositol phosphate head group (Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 / IP6). Replacing the arginine with histidine removes the positive charge and hydrogen-bonding contact, weakening lipid-headgroup recognition and so reducing membrane recruitment and activation.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E4", "E6", "E10", "E14", "E15", "E16"], "would_refute": "Ligand-bound PH-domain structures (for example 1B55 and 1BWN with 4IP) show R28 side chain not within contact distance of the inositol phosphate, and computed or measured binding free energy for R28H changes by less than about 0.5 kcal/mol.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "Ranked first because E4 (UniProt binding-site annotation at residue 28 for Ins(1,3,4,5,)P4, experimentally backed) and the ligand-bound crystal structures (E15, E16) are about this exact residue. E6 is a computed binding-energy study that argues for a binding effect over folding. Still missing: any experimental measurement of R28H binding affinity (G1), so this rests on annotation and simulation, not measurement."}

name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28H disrupts PH-TH domain dimerisation. The arginine at the dimer interface is lost, so the autoinhibitory PH-TH assembly needed for membrane-dependent activation of BTK cannot form, lowering activation in both membrane and cytosolic contexts.", "mechanism_class": "protein_interaction", "supports": ["E5", "E18", "E9", "E11"], "would_refute": "The R28 side chain is buried away from the PH-TH or homodimer interface in the 6TT2 and 1B55 crystal contacts and in a modelled PH-TH dimer, and an in-silico R28H model keeps the same interface contact energy and buried surface as wild type.", "starting_rank": 2, "rank_rationale": "Ranked second because the only activity-level evidence for R28H (E5, 2024 JBC) points to PH-TH dimerisation, but it is one study with no replication (G3), and the retrieved abstract does not give the interface residues. The E18 GTF2I interaction is unmapped (G6) and does not place R28 on any interface. The structural basis for R28 at a dimer interface is therefore unconfirmed."}

The high-resolution structures (E14 and others) have not yet been checked for buried contacts at residue 28."}
